lens: M2 — Zoomed-out fit: does this change belong in the system as architected, or is it parallel infrastructure that should be unified?
answer: Three of the four sub-checks (scorecard-render, consensus-debate-evidence, rust-default-language) land in the correct crate with explicit charter from ADR-0092 D13 and multispectrum-review.json FixupTask IDs. The fourth (naming-convention) creates a zoom-level mismatch: it enforces P14 BNF kebab-case naming of durable homes, a naming-governance concern that belongs in a dedicated oya-check-naming crate per ADR-0056 flat check-namespace design. The placement is extends-existing for three sub-checks but introduces a risk-of-drift vector as the crate accumulates unrelated process-compliance concerns under the dependency-seam label — a name that no longer describes the full scope at 10 sub-checks.
key_claims: ADR-0092 D13 explicitly charters oya-check-dependency-seam as the composite seam-discipline lane with 3+3 sub-checks; TG2 grows it to 10 — still within the lane's declared composite role per multispectrum-review.json#mandatory_subchecks_in_seam_lane and the enforced_by list in the spec.

multispectrum-review.json#consensus_debate_protocol#fixuptask_for_full_impl names F-LANE-DEBATE-SUBCHECK explicitly targeting oya-check-dependency-seam; check_consensus_debate_evidence is the correct home.
multispectrum-review.json#scorecard_schema#lane_implementation names F-LANE-SCORECARD-RENDER explicitly targeting oya-check-dependency-seam; check_scorecard_render is the correct home.

check_rust_default_language enforces P15 (rust-default-language policy) — a cross-cutting language-policy concern with no dedicated oya-check-language-policy crate yet; temporary placement here is acceptable under parallel-and-temporary classification, but FixupTask F-LANE-RUST-DEFAULT-ENFORCE should include crate-extraction as a deferred step.

check_naming_convention enforces P14 BNF kebab-case on durable homes (specs/, registries/, evidence/, templates/) — this is a naming-governance concern, not a dependency-seam concern. oya-check-naming or oya-check-adr-index are more natural homes per ADR-0056 flat check-namespace. This is the clearest zoom-level mismatch of the four.
ADR-0069 active-artifact-contract: all four sub-checks are consumers of ADR-0069 evidence bundle outputs. None implement a parallel artifact-contract capability model — fit is aligned, not parallel.
ADR-0056 12-layer enum + BNF: oya-check-dependency-seam is fully exempt from the 12-layer enum under the flat oya-check-rule-name namespace. No BNF violation in placing sub-checks here.
No industry primitive covers per-repo multispectrum sub-check composition at this granularity — no reinvention risk against AWS COE, Google Design Doc, Microsoft 1ES, or Oracle EngExc patterns.

At 1-year zoom: if oya-check-dependency-seam continues accumulating process-compliance sub-checks beyond seam-discipline, the crate name becomes a misleading catch-all. Correct long-term shape is to extract naming and language-policy checks to dedicated oya-check-* crates once they mature past NotYetArmed.
uncertainty_areas: Whether future extraction of naming-convention and rust-default-language into dedicated crates would require breaking CompositeReport consumers that bind by sub-check id string.
Whether multispectrum-review.json will formally extend mandatory_subchecks_in_seam_lane to cover all 10 sub-checks or redirect naming/language-policy checks to dedicated lanes.
existing_primitives_surveyed: oya-check-dependency-seam (ADR-0092 D13 charters composite seam-discipline lane)
industry_primitives_surveyed: cargo-deny (partial overlap with seam-imports; not a substitute for dependency-rationales.json isolation contracts)
fit_rationale: Two of four (scorecard-render, consensus-debate-evidence) are explicitly called out in multispectrum-review.json FixupTask IDs targeting oya-check-dependency-seam — unambiguously correct placement. check_rust_default_language is acceptable as parallel-and-temporary pending dedicated oya-check-language-policy crate. check_naming_convention is weakest fit: P14 BNF naming-governance is orthogonal to dependency-seam discipline — at 1-year zoom should migrate to oya-check-naming when it graduates from NotYetArmed.
